grand_strategy.reading: Cuba's strategy is to outlast the fuel blockade without changing its political order, and it keeps every channel open, from a Russian tanker and Vietnamese rice to a Mexican offer and Vatican mediation, while refusing to negotiate the system itself. Its means are thin: tourism run by foreign chains and a few diplomatic channels, against a US that has turned the fuel supply itself into the lever. The paradox is structural: the pressure meant to make Havana bend works through its suppliers, so each partner who hesitates leaves the grid darker and pushes more Cubans out.

stances.note: Havana's view as the press reports it: Díaz-Canel says there are no conversations with Washington beyond migration technicalities and that any external aggressor will face an impenetrable resistance (January 2026), and on 20 March 2026 Havana's line hardened to a refusal to negotiate the system. The structure is a fuel blockade and a stated wish, as reported, to remove the president. Rival, not adversary: Havana's aim is to defend its order and survive the pressure, not to see the United States destroyed, and no source reports a Cuban aim against the US state. Cooling since the January 2026 measures; the March talks are the one counter-movement. Bond grievance: the embargo and the 1959-62 rupture. Grade is our reading of the structure (C); the US side's stance is in data/stances/USA.yaml and is not copied.

stances_toward.note: Partner, cooling. Mexico supported the Cuban government from the early 1960s, abstained rather than backed the 1964 OAS expulsion, and kept relations when the rest of the hemisphere broke them: an ideological affinity, the basis of bond affinity. The cooling is the oil: Pemex shipped nearly 20,000 barrels a day to Cuba in Jan-Sep 2025, then Sheinbaum announced a pause on 27 Jan 2026, calling it a sovereign decision and declining to link it to US pressure after the Venezuela operation. Partner, not reluctant partner: the support is not forced on Mexico; the pause is the sign of how far the affinity bends under Washington. Confidence B on the 2026 pause; the 1960s affinity rests on the index (tier 4). Sharpened 2026-10-16 from the CUB card: Mexico has sent no fuel since the US executive order of January 2026 (Reuters, 13 May 2026); Sheinbaum said in February that the US oil block could cause a humanitarian crisis, and in June 2026 said Mexico wanted to restart shipments through commercial and private firms with no timeline. The CUB card reads Mexico as partner, trend cooling, bond none (our reading, no source names kinship); Mexico keeps bond affinity from the 1960s record. The June offer is the counter-signal, so the trend stays cooling but the question is open.

Washington re-listed Cuba as a state sponsor of terrorism on inauguration day, killed 32 Cuban security personnel in the Caracas raid, declared Cuba an 'unusual and extraordinary threat' and authorised tariffs on any country selling it oil (29 Jan 2026, a fuel blockade in the words of UN experts), and Trump said Cuba 'looks ready to fall' and that he would have 'the honor' of taking it 'in some form'. Yet both governments confirmed high-level talks on 13 Mar 2026 and Washington's instrument is strangulation, not a declared war aim of ending the state; the grade follows the structure and would become adversary with a declared regime-change operation. Cooling. Bond - grievance: 1959-62 as Washington tells it. Cuba has no card yet.

stances_toward.note: The old alliance turned into a transaction under pressure. Cuba was Venezuela's oil client under the 2000 accord (oil for services; 26,500 bpd in 2025, about a third of the island's need, per a secondary analysis that is not audited), and 32 Cuban security personnel died in the raid of 3 Jan 2026. From January Venezuela stopped sending crude to Cuba under US pressure, and Washington threatened tariffs on any third country that supplies Cuban oil (executive order of 29 Jan 2026, as recorded on the USA card). Partner, not ally, because the accord has no living oil flow and Caracas now has no oil to give (our reading). Cooling because the supply stopped. Bond affinity: the shared revolutionary inheritance, the security ties and the Cuban dead. Confidence C: no Venezuelan statement on the cut was read; the grade is our reading of the structure, and the Cuban card will check it from the other side.
